Notes: Script data/rankings/fairvote_cvr.py (source file Minneapolis_20091106_BoardofTaxationAtLarge.tab). Design record data/rankings/design_tables.csv. Not on Redivis yet. Checked against the city's own 2009 cast vote record for this contest (identical ballots). The city counted by hand, on ballots rewritten by its Voter Error Accounting Chart: an overvote or a duplicate ranking ended the ballot at that ranking, one skipped ranking was closed up, and two skipped rankings in a row left a blank ballot. The recount rules are: one skipped ranking is passed over, a ballot that has skipped more than one (1) ranking ends there, and an overvote or a duplicate ranking ends the ballot (Code 167.60(a)(2) and 167.70(a)(2), where 2008-Or-028 and 2009-Or-102 agree on the skipped ranking; 2009-Or-102 was adopted on 2 October 2009 and signed by the mayor on 7 October 2009). A recount from this table with these rules reproduces every round of the city's tabulation sheet except for the difference below. The city defeated several candidates at once (batch elimination, Code 167.20 and 167.70(a)(1)c): a candidate whose votes plus every vote that could still reach them would not pass the next higher candidate is defeated with all candidates below. Notes: Script data/rankings/fairvote_cvr.py (source file Alaska_20220816_USHouse_Special.tab). Design record data/rankings/design_tables.csv. Not on Redivis yet. Checked against the Division of Elections' own 2022 cast vote record for this contest (identical ballots). The file holds 192289 ballots, 253 fewer than the Division's Times Cast of 192542: its cast vote record "does not include ballots that were only counted by hand", and its RCV Detailed Report counts the same 192289. No candidate had more than one-half of the active ballots on first choices, so the Division tabulated the contest in rounds, one candidate defeated per round until two remained (AS 15.15.350(d)). A recount from this table, with the ballots that have no mark (and so no rows) counted among the Blanks, reproduces every round of the Division's RCV Detailed Report (2 rounds, with each candidate's votes, the inactive ballots and the winner) when an overvote makes the ballot inactive when the count reaches it, one skipped ranking is passed over and a second in a row makes the ballot inactive, a later ranking of a candidate already ranked counts as a skipped ranking, and the write-in marks, taken as one line because write-in candidates filed for the race, are defeated before round 1 under 6 AAC 25.071 (the active ballots on which a write-in candidate ranked highest fell short of the leading candidate's votes by at least 0.5 percent of the two together) and then passed over. Every round is reproduced only when, in addition, a repeated write-in mark counts as a duplicate ranking, as the Division's cast vote record flags it (DuplicatedRcvCandidate): without that convention 2 ballots, each ranking the write-in line three times and then a candidate or an overvote, are counted for that candidate or as an overvote, where the report counts them among its Blanks. A second counting program, written from the statute and regulation texts and the Division's definitions of its tabulation options (its 2022 media packet), without sight of the first program's code and set to the first program's readings at the two points, among those the texts leave open, where it first read the texts otherwise (whether a disregarded duplicate ranking is a skipped ranking, and whether write-in candidates defeated under 6 AAC 25.071 keep a line in round 1), gives the first program's tallies in every round without that convention.

Notes: Script data/rankings/fairvote_cvr.py (source file Alaska_20221108_HouseDistrict11.tab). Design record data/rankings/design_tables.csv. Not on Redivis yet. Checked against the Division of Elections' own 2022 cast vote record for this contest (identical ballots). The file holds 8190 ballots, the Division's Times Cast for the contest and the total of its RCV Detailed Report. No candidate had more than one-half of the active ballots on first choices, so the Division tabulated the contest in rounds, one candidate defeated per round until two remained (AS 15.15.350(d)). A recount from this table, with the ballots that have no mark (and so no rows) counted among the Blanks, reproduces every round of the Division's RCV Detailed Report (2 rounds, with each candidate's votes, the inactive ballots and the winner) when an overvote makes the ballot inactive when the count reaches it, one skipped ranking is passed over and a second in a row makes the ballot inactive, a later ranking of a candidate already ranked counts as a skipped ranking, and a write-in mark counts for nobody and is passed over, as no write-in candidate filed for the race. A second counting program, written from the statute and regulation texts and the Division's definitions of its tabulation options (its 2022 media packet), without sight of the first program's code, gives the same tallies in every round once it is set to the first program's readings at the two points, among those the texts leave open, where it first read the texts otherwise (whether a disregarded duplicate ranking is a skipped ranking, and whether write-in candidates defeated under 6 AAC 25.071 keep a line in round 1).
